headline: High-risk shared filesystem and clipboard bridge create prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict exposure; pdf.js adds a browser-based parsing surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read/write workspace files and clipboard contents, and its shared state with other instances is via the local filesystem. pdf.js reads PDF files in a browser-based worker model. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled document content or copied text is treated as instructions, though not a guaranteed direct channel.
conditions: IF Cursor opens or copies content originating from a PDF that contains instruction-like text
IF the operator moves text between the two agents via clipboard or shared files
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Keep pdf.js outputs in a separate folder from Cursor workspaces
Review PDF-derived text before pasting into Cursor
Use read-only exports from pdf.js
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and can use broad network egress plus model providers. pdf.js touches PDF documents and has no network egress. If both share a local filesystem, sensitive PDF content can be opened in Cursor and then transmitted to third-party model providers, creating a realistic exfiltration path.
conditions: IF PDF documents contain sensitive or regulated data
IF Cursor is allowed to send open-file context to external model providers
mitigations: Store sensitive PDFs outside Cursor workspaces
Turn off external model provider routing for sensitive sessions
Open PDFs in a separate non-shared directory
Redact sensitive pages before import
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on outbound prompts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git-state modification, and broad network egress; pdf.js reads PDF files and runs in a browser-based test/worker model. Because Cursor explicitly shares state via the local filesystem, both can mutate overlapping files without locking, making concurrent corruption or git conflicts likely in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF Cursor auto-runs commands or edits files while pdf.js is processing PDFs
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Avoid concurrent git operations
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add workspace-level coordination/locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can generate code or facts from open files, and pdf.js can present parsed PDF content that Cursor may treat as authoritative. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so errors from PDF parsing or extracted text can cascade into Cursor actions, but pdf.js itself does not take downstream actions.
conditions: IF Cursor uses PDF-derived text as source material without manual verification
IF extracted PDF content is copied into Cursor-generated code or notes
mitigations: Verify PDF-derived claims against the original document
Mark extracted text as untrusted input
Require human review before Cursor acts on PDF content
Keep citations linked to page numbers
requires-engineering: add structured provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Cursor is closed-source and handles model-provider API keys, while pdf.js is open-source and local-browser oriented; the available profiles do not show a concrete compliance conflict, so only a low, documentation-gap risk remains.
conditions: IF the deployment routes regulated data through Cursor to external model providers
IF an operator assumes pdf.js and Cursor share the same retention policy without checking
mitigations: Review vendor privacy terms before use
Keep regulated PDFs out of Cursor sessions
Disable external provider calls for sensitive work
Document retention settings for both tools
requires-engineering: formalize a data-handling policy
